While policy tools such as the Domestic Content Bonus under the investment tax credit and production tax credit create important levers for reshoring LPT manufacturing, their effectiveness hinges on parallel investments in upstream inputs, skilled workforce training, and expansion of U.S. assembly infrastructure. Federal policy developments in 2024 and 2025 provide new opportunities to offset these vulnerabilities. The Domestic Content Bonus credit extended tax incentive eligibility to hydropower and PSH projects, and IRS Notice 2024-41 and Notice 2025-08 made it easier to use. Safe harbor provisions now allow industry to rely on IRS-accepted classifications for wind, solar, and battery electric storage systems, while the 80/20 retrofit rule enables qualifying rehabilitation projects to benefit from the incentive. Generator step-up transformers are explicitly included as manufactured products, and recent 2025 guidance further tightened restrictions on sourcing from FEOC countries, reshaping procurement practices. Taken together, these measures not only improve the economics of hydropower and PSH projects through up to a 10% credit boost but also create strong incentives to expand domestic manufacturing and supply capacity. Given the strategic significance of U.S. hydropower infrastructure, and especially as hydropower emerges as a solution to meet the growing demand for firm, flexible power, sustained federal support and public/private sector cooperation will be essential to secure a steady supply of LPTs. In the near term, utilities and hydropower plant operators are placing transformer orders much earlier, sharing spare parts, gradually updating outdated equipment, and advocating for supportive regulatory frameworks. Through higher utilization of current manufacturing facilities alongside investing in workforce training programs, existing domestic transformer manufacturers can help address some of the immediate supply challenges.
